public_rationale: On the ordinary release-gap reading, the claim holds. GPT-4 was released on March 14, 2023, placing Marcus's post two years, two months and eight days later. Contemporary reporting still described GPT-5 as forthcoming in April 2025; OpenAI's subsequent launch announcement is dated August 7, 2025. This supports the statement about the public wait. It does not establish that GPT-5 underwent more than two years of internal development.
limitations: The starting point and the meaning of 'well over' are evaluator interpretations.
The contemporary status report predates the post by several weeks; the later primary launch announcement corroborates the chronology.
This assessment concerns the named model's public release, not intervening technical progress or the feasibility of AI 2027.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: GPT-5 is still not here and has taken well over two years.

statement.excerpt: Agent 3, “augmenting the AI’s text-based scratchpad (chain of thought) with a higher-bandwidth thought process (neuralese recurrence and memory)” is pegged to arrive just 3 months later (never mind that GPT-5, still not here, has taken well over two years).
statement.document_title: The “AI 2027” Scenario: How realistic is it?

from_speaker: has taken well over two years
our_interpretation: Read 'still not here' as not publicly released by the post date, May 22, 2025.
Read 'has taken' as elapsed waiting time since GPT-4's public release, rather than a claim about the duration of internal training or development.
The target period covers that elapsed interval, from GPT-4's release through the post date.
Read 'well over two years' ordinarily as months beyond the second anniversary; Marcus supplies no exact margin.
criteria.support_condition: GPT-5 remained publicly unreleased on May 22, 2025, and GPT-4's public release preceded that date by more than two years with a margin measured in months.
criteria.contradiction_condition: GPT-5 was publicly released by May 22, 2025, or the elapsed interval since GPT-4's public release did not exceed two years by months.
